questions.q: If A and B are finite sets and $A \subset B$, then
questions.explanation: Since $A \subset B$, $A \cup B = B$, so $n(A \cup B) = n(B)$.

questions.q: The value of $\cos^2 45^\circ - \sin^2 15^\circ$ is
questions.explanation: $\cos^2A-\sin^2B=\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)=\cos60^\circ\cos30^\circ=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}$.

questions.q: $3+5+7+\ldots$ to n terms is
questions.explanation: This is an AP with first term 3 and common difference 2; sum $=\dfrac n2[2(3)+(n-1)2]=n(n+2)$.

questions.q: If $\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^m=1$, then the least positive integral value of m is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}=i$, and $i^m=1$ needs the least positive $m=4$.

questions.q: If $|x-2|\le1$, then
questions.explanation: $|x-2|\le1$ gives $1\le x\le3$, i.e. $x\in[1,3]$.

questions.q: If ${}^nC_{12}={}^nC_8$ then n is equal to
questions.explanation: ${}^nC_r={}^nC_s$ with $r\ne s$ implies $n=r+s=12+8=20$.

questions.q: The total number of terms in the expansion of $(x+a)^{47}-(x-a)^{47}$ after simplification is
questions.explanation: Only terms with odd powers of $a$ survive, giving $\dfrac{47+1}{2}=24$ terms.

questions.q: Equation of line passing through the point $(1,2)$ and perpendicular to the line $y=3x-1$ is
questions.explanation: Slope of the given line is 3, so the perpendicular slope is $-\dfrac13$; the line through $(1,2)$ is $y-2=-\dfrac13(x-1) \Rightarrow x+3y-7=0$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to0}\dfrac{1-\cos4\theta}{1-\cos6\theta}$ is
questions.explanation: Using $1-\cos k\theta\approx \dfrac{k^2\theta^2}{2}$, the limit is $\dfrac{16}{36}=\dfrac49$.

questions.q: The contrapositive statement of the statement "If x is prime number, then x is odd" is
options: If x is not a prime number, then x is not odd
If x is a prime number, then x is not odd.
If x is not a prime number, then x is odd.
If x is not odd, then x is not a prime number.
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of "if p then q" is "if not q then not p": "If x is not odd, then x is not a prime number."

questions.q: If coefficient of variation is 60 and standard deviation is 24, then Arithmetic mean is
questions.explanation: $CV=\dfrac{\sigma}{\bar x}\times100 \Rightarrow 60=\dfrac{24}{\bar x}\times100 \Rightarrow \bar x=40$.

questions.q: The range of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{9-x^2}$ is
questions.explanation: For $x\in[-3,3]$, $f(x)$ ranges from $0$ (at $x=\pm3$) to $3$ (at $x=0$), giving $[0,3]$.

questions.q: Let $f:R\to R$ be defined by $f(x)=x^4$, then
options: f may be one-one and onto
f is one-one but not onto
f is neither one-one nor onto
questions.explanation: $f(x)=x^4$ gives $f(1)=f(-1)$ (not one-one) and never takes negative values (not onto R).

questions.q: The range of $\sec^{-1}x$ is
questions.explanation: By definition the range of $\sec^{-1}x$ is $[0,\pi]$ excluding $\pi/2$.

questions.q: If a matrix A is both symmetric and skew symmetric, then
questions.explanation: $A=A^T$ and $A=-A^T$ together force $A=-A$, so every entry is 0, i.e. A is the zero matrix.

questions.q: If $2\begin{bmatrix}1&3\\0&x\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}y&0\\1&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5&6\\1&8\end{bmatrix}$, then the value of x and y are
questions.explanation: Comparing entries: $2+y=5\Rightarrow y=3$, and $2x+2=8\Rightarrow x=3$.

questions.q: Binary operation $*$ on $R-\{-1\}$ defined by $a*b=\dfrac{a}{b+1}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $a*b=\dfrac{a}{b+1}\ne \dfrac{b}{a+1}=b*a$ in general, and $(a*b)*c\ne a*(b*c)$ in general, the operation is neither commutative nor associative.

questions.q: If $\begin{vmatrix}3&x\\x&1\end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix}3&2\\4&1\end{vmatrix}$ then x is equal to
questions.explanation: $3-x^2=3-8=-5\Rightarrow x^2=8\Rightarrow x=\pm2\sqrt2$.

questions.q: If A is a square matrix of order $3\times3$, then $|KA|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: For an $n\times n$ matrix, $|KA|=K^n|A|$; here $n=3$, so $|KA|=K^3|A|$.

questions.q: The area of triangle with vertices $(K,0), (4,0), (0,2)$ is 4 square units, then value of K is
Let $\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}Ax&x^2&1\\By&y^2&1\\Cz&z^2&1\end{vmatrix}$ and $\Delta_1=\begin{vmatrix}A&B&C\\x&y&z\\zy&zx&xy\end{vmatrix}$ then
questions.explanation: Expanding both determinants and using column operations to factor out $xyz$ shows $\Delta_1=\Delta$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\begin{cases}Kx^2 & x\le2\\3 & x>2\end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=2$, then the value of K is
questions.explanation: Continuity requires $K(2)^2=3\Rightarrow4K=3\Rightarrow K=3/4$.

questions.q: The value of C in Mean value theorem for the function $f(x)=x^2$ in $[2,4]$ is
The point on the curve $y^2=x$ where the tangent makes an angle of $\pi/4$ with X-axis is
questions.explanation: $2y\,dy/dx=1\Rightarrow dy/dx=\dfrac{1}{2y}=\tan(\pi/4)=1\Rightarrow y=\dfrac12,\ x=y^2=\dfrac14$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=x^2+2x-5$ is strictly increasing in the interval
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=2x+2>0$ when $x>-1$, so f is strictly increasing on $(-1,\infty)$.

questions.q: The rate of change of volume of a sphere with respect to its surface area when the radius is 4 cm is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dV}{dS}=\dfrac{dV/dr}{dS/dr}=\dfrac{4\pi r^2}{8\pi r}=\dfrac r2=2\ cm^3/cm^2$ at $r=4$.

questions.q: If $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{\cos x-\sin x}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $y=\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+x\right)\right)=\dfrac\pi4+x$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1$.

questions.q: If $y=\begin{vmatrix}f(x)&g(x)&h(x)\\l&m&n\\a&b&c\end{vmatrix}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since rows 2 and 3 are constants, only row 1 is differentiated, giving option A; a cyclic permutation of the rows (option D) and the transpose (option C) leave the determinant's value unchanged, so KEA accepted A, C and D.

questions.q: If $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, $\tan y=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Both expressions equal $\sin(2\tan^{-1}t)$ and $\tan(2\tan^{-1}t)$ respectively, giving $x=y=2\tan^{-1}t$, so $dy/dx=1$.

questions.q: The derivative of $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)$ w.r.t $\cos^{-1}x$ is
questions.explanation: Since $\cos^{-1}(2x^2-1)=2\cos^{-1}x$, its derivative with respect to $\cos^{-1}x$ is simply 2.

questions.q: If $y=\log(\log x)$ then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $y'=\dfrac{1}{x\log x}$; differentiating again with the quotient rule gives $y''=\dfrac{-(1+\log x)}{(x\log x)^2}$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{(x+3)e^x}{(x+4)^2}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Writing the integrand as $e^x\left[\dfrac{1}{x+4}-\dfrac{1}{(x+4)^2}\right]$ matches $e^x[f(x)+f'(x)]$ with $f(x)=\dfrac1{x+4}$, so the integral is $\dfrac{e^x}{x+4}+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\cos2x-\cos2\theta}{\cos x-\cos\theta}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $\cos2x-\cos2\theta=2(\cos x-\cos\theta)(\cos x+\cos\theta)$, so the integrand simplifies to $2(\cos x+\cos\theta)$, giving $2(\sin x+x\cos\theta)+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^2+2x+5}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Writing $x^2+2x+5=(x+1)^2+2^2$ and using the standard formula $\int\sqrt{u^2+a^2}\,du$ gives $\dfrac12(x+1)\sqrt{x^2+2x+5}+2\log|x+1+\sqrt{x^2+2x+5}|+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\tan^7x}{\cot^7x+\tan^7x}\,dx$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $\int_0^a f(x)dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)dx$ with $a=\pi/2$, the integral equals its own complement, so it equals half of $\pi/2$, i.e. $\pi/4$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-5}^{5}|x+2|\,dx$ is equal to
$\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{e^{\sin x}+1}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Since $f(x)+f(-x)=1$ here, the integral equals half the length of the interval, $\dfrac12\cdot\pi=\dfrac\pi2$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{a^2\sin^2x+b^2\cos^2x}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is a standard result: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{a^2\sin^2x+b^2\cos^2x}=\dfrac{\pi}{2ab}$.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^2$ and the line $y=16$ is
questions.explanation: By symmetry, area $=2\int_0^4(16-x^2)dx=2\left[16x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^4=\dfrac{256}{3}$ sq units.

questions.q: Area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\cos x$, $x=0$ and $x=\pi$ is
questions.explanation: Area $=\left|\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos x\,dx\right|+\left|\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi}\cos x\,dx\right|=1+1=2$ sq units.

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation $\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^2=\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is
questions.explanation: The highest order derivative $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ occurs to the power 1, so the degree is 1.

questions.q: General solution of differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=1\ (y\ne1)$ is
questions.explanation: Separating variables, $\dfrac{dy}{1-y}=dx$; integrating gives $-\log|1-y|=x+C$, i.e. $\log\left|\dfrac{1}{1-y}\right|=x+C$.

questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation $x\cdot\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x^2$ is $(x\ne0)$
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac2xy=x$, the integrating factor is $e^{\int(2/x)dx}=e^{2\log x}=x^2$.

questions.q: If $\vec a=2\hat i+\lambda\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ are orthogonal, then value of $\lambda$ is
questions.explanation: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=2+2\lambda+3=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-\dfrac52$.

questions.q: If $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are unit vectors such that $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, then the value of $\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=0=3+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)$, giving the sum $=-\dfrac32$.

questions.q: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are unit vectors, then angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ for $\sqrt3\vec a-\vec b$ to be a unit vector is
questions.explanation: $|\sqrt3\vec a-\vec b|^2=3+1-2\sqrt3\cos\theta=1\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$.

questions.q: Reflexion of the point $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ in XY plane is
questions.explanation: Reflection in the XY-plane keeps x and y unchanged and reverses the sign of z.

questions.q: The plane $2x-3y+6z-11=0$ makes an angle $\sin^{-1}(\alpha)$ with X-axis. The value of $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.explanation: The normal vector $(2,-3,6)$ has magnitude 7; the angle the plane makes with the x-axis satisfies $\sin\alpha=\dfrac{|2|}{7}=\dfrac27$.

questions.q: The distance of the point $(-2,4,-5)$ from the line $\dfrac{x+3}{3}=\dfrac{y-4}{5}=\dfrac{z+8}{6}$ is
questions.explanation: Taking the vector from the line's point $(-3,4,-8)$ to the given point, $(1,0,3)$, and removing its component along the direction $(3,5,6)$, the perpendicular component has magnitude $\sqrt{37/10}$.

questions.q: A box has 100 pens of which 10 are defective. The probability that out of a sample of 5 pens drawn one by one with replacement and atmost one is defective is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{at most 1 defective})=P(0)+P(1)=(0.9)^5+{}^5C_1(0.1)(0.9)^4=\left(\dfrac9{10}\right)^5+\dfrac12\left(\dfrac9{10}\right)^4$.

questions.q: Two events A and B will be independent if
options: A and B are mutually exclusive
questions.explanation: $A,B$ are independent $\iff$ $A',B'$ are independent $\iff$ $P(A'\cap B')=P(A')P(B')=(1-P(A))(1-P(B))$.

questions.q: The probability distribution of X is: X = 0, 1, 2, 3 with P(X) = 0.3, k, 2k, 2k respectively. The value of k is
questions.explanation: Sum of probabilities is 1: $0.3+k+2k+2k=1\Rightarrow5k=0.7\Rightarrow k=0.14$.

questions.q: [Figure: a line through (0,5) and (4,0) forms a triangle-like boundary with a horizontal line through (0,3) and a vertical line through (6,0); the shaded region is the triangular area between the slanted line, below y=3 and left of x=6.] The shaded region in the figure is the solution set of the inequations
questions.explanation: The line through $(0,5)$ and $(4,0)$ is $5x+4y=20$; the shaded region lies on the outer side of this line, below $y=3$ and left of $x=6$, i.e. $5x+4y\ge20, x\le6, y\le3, x\ge0, y\ge0$.

questions.q: If an LPP admits optimal solution at two consecutive vertices of a feasible region, then
options: the required optimal solution is at the midpoint of the line joining two points.
the optimal solution occurs at every point on the line joining these two points
the LPP under consideration is not solvable
the LPP under consideration must be reconstructed
questions.explanation: When two adjacent vertices give the same optimal value, every point on the segment joining them is also optimal.
